title: A focused weekly marketing hour and a network map
audience: Solo practitioners and small teams who struggle to find time for marketing
learningOutcomes: Choose one marketing task for a fixed weekly hour and prepare for it in advance
Map personal and professional contacts into closeness tiers, with consent and contact notes
Review a task after four weeks and stop it if it produces no result

instruction.heading: Protect a fixed hour
instruction.body: Marketing often loses out to client work. A fixed weekly hour, with one task and no distractions, produces more than scattered effort. Prepare the materials the day before: the list, the message, the contact details, the venue address. Choose the task most likely to create an enquiry that week. Examples include sending the newsletter, sending personal messages to clients who have said yes to receiving your updates, or visiting nearby businesses to introduce yourself.

instruction.heading: Map your network
instruction.body: Your network includes people who know your work well, people who know you a little, and people who know of you. List them and mark the closeness of each relationship. Note how each person could open a door: by referring a client, hosting a talk, or passing on your details. Record the consent status and the last contact date. Do not send promotional messages to the whole list.

instruction.heading: Measure the output
instruction.body: After each hour, record what it produced: messages sent, conversations started, meetings held. Review after four weeks. A task with no measurable output should be changed or stopped, not repeated from habit.

procedure: Choose one weekly slot and one task for it.
Prepare the list, the message and any materials before the slot begins.
Write the network list in three closeness tiers, with a note on how each contact could help.
Log the output of each hour.
After four weeks, keep, change or stop each task.

workedExamples.situation: A hypothetical trainer has an hour each Thursday and has tried three tasks: a newsletter, personal texts to members, and calls to local clinics.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which task should keep the slot after four weeks?
workedExamples.reasoning: Compare the logged output. The task that started conversations or meetings with a measurable result should keep the slot. A task that started no conversations should be changed or stopped. The decision rests on the log, not on how much effort the task felt like.

equipmentAndPpe: Network list (spreadsheet with closeness, consent and last-contact columns)

commonErrors.error: Planning the hour and never doing the task
commonErrors.prevention: Prepare materials the day before and begin when the slot opens.

commonErrors.error: A network list with no notes
commonErrors.prevention: Record closeness, consent and last contact for each name.

commonErrors.error: Sending promotional messages to people who have not said yes to receiving messages from you
commonErrors.prevention: Check consent first, and follow “Keeping in touch: newsletters and a consent-based contact plan”.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Individual promotional messages may be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003.

qualityStandard: The hour is scheduled and the task is logged every week
Each contact has a closeness tier and a consent note
A keep, change or stop decision is recorded after four weeks
summary: Map the network by closeness, with consent notes.
Keep, change or stop each task after four weeks.

knowledgeChecks.question: The main purpose of a fixed marketing hour is to:
options: Complete one chosen marketing task without distraction
Test advertising across several channels at the same time

knowledgeChecks.question: When mapping a network, the lesson suggests grouping contacts by:
options: Age and postcode only, since those fields are easy to sort
How close the relationship is and how each person could open a door
How much they spend and how often they visit the gym each week

knowledgeChecks.question: After four weeks, a task that has produced no output should be:
options: Kept running indefinitely, because the cost is low each week
Reviewed, and changed or stopped if it still produces nothing
Given double the time each week, so the result has longer to show

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: Says commercial messages cannot be sent without the recipient's permission or consent; messages must accurately identify the sender and include correct contact details; every commercial message must contain an unsubscribe option under the Spam Act 2003, which the page says sets out responsibilities under Australian law. Does not mention one-to-one messages. Publisher: ACMA.
